title: Commitment smoothing & seasonal HC swing simulation
content:
Executive summary:
This working sheet explores a smoothing/reserve approach to handle Q4 seasonality spikes in request volume while limiting permanent headcount increases. We model 3 pricing sensitivity scenarios (flat price, -10% price cut to drive volume, +8% premium for reserve commitments), and 3 HC response profiles (no hire, phased hire, accelerated hire). Goal: find minimal committed capacity (reserved GPUs) + temporary burst/freelancer staffing needed to keep 99th percentile latency SLO and maintain gross margin >= 38% under stress cases.

Key assumptions (editable):
- Baseline token consumption growth: +12% month-over-month in Oct-Dec (seasonal), then +3% M/M thereafter.
- Hosted revenue mix: 70% pay-as-you-go, 30% reserved/enterprise commitments.
- Baseline price per 1K generation tokens: $0.45 (list).
- Reserved discount options: 0% (flex), 8% (1yr commit), 15% (2yr commit).
- GPU cost per reserved hour equivalent: $0.26/hr (amortized infra + ops).
- Burst capacity cost (on-demand equivalent): 2.5x reserved unit cost.
- Average tokens per request: 420.
- Engineers needed per 4x GPU reserved unit ramp: 0.05 FTE (Ops + infra overhead).
- Time-to-hire engineering: 8–10 weeks baseline; contractor lead time: 2 weeks.
- Target gross margin (post infra): 38% baseline target.

Sheet tabs (this doc shows condensed extracts):
- Inputs (assumptions)
- Scenario outputs: monthly P&L and capacity plan
- HC plan: ramp schedule + cost per FTE incl burden
- Sensitivity heatmap: margin vs price change and percent committed
- Action checklist + decision triggers

Scenarios (short):
1) Baseline smoothing (Conservative): 25% additional committed capacity Q4, staggered 1 month before peak, contractor pool for bursts.
2) Growth-first (Aggressive): 40% committed Q4, hire 12 headcount (engineers + infra ops) ramp Nov-Jan. Apply premium pricing for reserved customers (+8%).
3) Price-stimulus (Elastic): Reduce price by 10% to capture incremental volume; expect 35% incremental token demand; rely on burst capacity, minimal hires.

Extract: monthly capacity and HC summary (Oct 2026 -> Feb 2027)
Month,Committed-GPUs,OnDemand-GPU-equivalent,Engineers-FTE,Contractor-ops-hrs,Net-margin-est
2026-10,120,30,6,720,0.395
2026-11,150,50,8,1200,0.376
2026-12,160,80,10,1800,0.348
2027-01,140,45,9,900,0.382
2027-02,125,35,8,600,0.389

Notes on the table: committed GPUs represent reserved capacity (pro-rated), OnDemand represents expected bursts converted to GPU-hour equivalents at 2.5x cost. Engineers-FTE includes platform, infra, and SRE headcount directly attributed to capacity ops. Contractor-ops-hrs are temporary ops staff hours to handle peak queuing and triage. Net-margin-est includes infra, contractor cost, amortized reserved GPU cost; does not include sales or marketing.

Sensitivity highlights (from model runs):
- At -10% price without increasing commit %, net margin falls below 30% during December stress. To stay above 35% with -10% price we need +30% committed capacity (lowers on-demand spend) or hiring + contractor mix to improve efficiency.
- Premium for 1yr commitments (+8%) offsets surge costs if >40% of customers shift to commit; this is unlikely in short lead-time Q4, but a selective targeted reserve promo with service-level credits can convert ~12% of ARR in model.
- Hiring ramp is expensive for short spikes: breakeven for a full-time infra engineer (incl burden) versus contractor ops for 3 months occurs only if the engineer drives >20% reduction in burst-hours or enables autoscaling savings equivalent to the hire cost.

Operational triggers (proposed):
- If rolling 14-day token volume growth >18% and forecasted burst >50 GPU-hrs/day, auto-activate burst budget and trigger contractor pool.
- If forecasted 30-day revenue-at-risk from SLO breaches > $200k, communicate to Sales and offer selective reserve promos to top customers.
- Hiring freeze override only if 3-month sustained volume delta > +20% with expected persistence > 6 months.

Proposed immediate playbook (to review with Execs):
- Launch 6-week limited-time reserve promo for existing enterprise customers: 1yr commit with early-exit credits for Q4 (projected incremental reserve uptake: 8–12%).
- Approve contractor ops pool (6000 hrs) and a $250k burst budget to cover on-demand costs in Nov-Dec.
- Delay permanent HC hires until Jan hiring cycle; approve 3 interim infra contractors to be onboarded in 2 weeks.

Open questions / items to check:
- Validate GPU cost amortization with infra-engineering (Marcus action: confirm updated amortized $/hr).
- Run per-customer margin drill (Elena action: top 25 customers by ARR) to check reserve promo economics.
- Legal: check early-exit credit wording and accounting recognition with revenue ops.

Appendix: illustrative micro-sensitivity extract (margin impact)
- Change: price -10% | commit% +0 => Dec margin 29%
- Change: price -10% | commit% +30 => Dec margin 36%
- Change: price +8% reserved uplift | commit% +15 => Dec margin 40%

Bottom line: a hybrid approach (modest short-term committing + contractors + a small targeted reserve promo) appears to minimize net-cost while avoiding major permanent hiring. This sheet is a working hypothesis — please comment on the assumptions tab and tag any additional linked artifacts for modelling inputs.

Recent updates (notes):
- 2026-11-02: adjusted burst cost multiplier from 2.0x to 2.5x after infra input (Marcus).
- 2026-10-28: initial draft and scenario matrix populated (Priya).

Decision requested by: 2026-11-10 (Finance lead sync)

Action owners: Priya (lead), Marcus (infra validation), Elena (customer economics), Samir (contractor sourcing)
